bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Disruption in the mobility industry - single-industry and passenger-car concentration — The Company's current revenues are generated from the automotive and mobility ecosystem and in particular the passenger-car segment. The cyclical nature of, or disruption in, the automotive industry, cost pressures, global slowdown and regulatory changes globally can hit growth and profitability. This is the AR's own top-listed risk and it is a structural concentration, not a cyclical one: the Company's stated differentiator - singular focus on mobility - is the same thing as its concentration. Mitigation is monitoring industry software spend and AI adoption, creating differentiated offerings, evaluating adjacent verticals, new geographies and market-specific solutions, aligning investment to client software spend, and partnerships for specific skills. The CEO's letter puts a near-term edge on it: two of the largest software-defined-vehicle programs wind down in H1 FY27.
- Technology disruption, especially AI, to the business model itself — Technology changes and the emergence of new and disruptive technologies, especially AI, can disrupt the Company's own business model. The Board's Report is explicit that AI-led adoption may in the near term MODERATE activity in certain service areas - i.e. the Company's own AI deployment can cannibalise billable effort before it pays back. Mitigation is investment in technology competencies with a major focus on AI reviewed through Practice Development Forums, continuous evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies and AI-infused business models, new offerings, and periodic strengthening of product strategy for development, validation and networking tools supporting clients' SDV transition.
- Delivery excellence - programme execution risk on client production programs — The work KPIT does is critical to clients' production programs; delays may impact those production programs, in an industry becoming more competitive with stricter vehicle safety and emission regulation, energy pressures and slower demand. Mitigation is agile delivery models, competency building with a focus on AI, zero-defect delivery, SCALE through automation and engineering productivity, proactive planning and process automation, and multi-level delivery reviews. The commercial mix amplifies this: more than 70% of new contracts are fixed-price, so execution slippage lands on KPIT's margin rather than the client's.
- Top talent retention and attraction — Ability to attract and retain talent, especially competence in new technology areas including AI, is key to maintaining leadership. The growing trajectory of Global Capability Centers in recent years may also create a challenge in retaining key talent; higher attrition may impact delivery and the ability to pursue growth opportunities. Mitigation is a strengthened talent acquisition and retention framework, continuous training and certification including AI, leadership development programs and individual development plans, and an employee engagement and recognition framework focused on top talent.
- Inability to grow key clients / revenue concentration, including the OEM Global Capability Centre threat — Inability to execute strategy will impact growth; OEMs driving major business through their own Global Capability Centers may also hit the Company's growth. This is the disintermediation risk - the client insourcing the work. Mitigation is strong strategic relationships with OEMs and top clients, a 'strategy for disrupters', a client engagement transformation program with proactive propositions and AI-infused solutions, understanding client technology roadmaps to prioritise investments, and a strategy for new offerings focused on Commercial Vehicles and Off-Highway verticals.
- Profitability compression from client spending patterns, pricing pressure and people cost — Profitability is significantly influenced by clients' spending patterns, competitive pricing pressure and increasing employee and other operational costs; lower profitability may impact sustainability and future investments. People cost is stated as the Company's significant cost. Mitigation is a focus on solutions and products, productivity improvement through AI and the employee pyramid, leveraging the global delivery model with an increase in offshore and nearshore mix, and investment in AI solutions, tools and automation.
- Major currency fluctuation - foreign-exchange exposure on overwhelmingly overseas revenue — Significant currency fluctuations impact financial results, and the Board's Report notes the Company's significant exposure to overseas revenues, so FX moves may affect revenues, profitability and overall financial performance; exposure extends to broader commodity trends including gold, crude oil and energy prices as drivers of currency volatility. Mitigation is a board-approved prudent forex hedging policy reviewed periodically, implementation overseen by the CFO, appropriate hedging product selection, continuous monitoring of currency movements and periodic recalibration of hedge positions.
- Economic and political risk, global trade policy and geopolitical conflict — Both the Company and its clients have a global footprint. Slowdown or recession in key geographies, prolonged geopolitical conflicts, trade-policy changes, supply-chain disruption and inflationary pressure may raise the cost of doing business and influence client decisions and spend. The Board's Report singles out evolving tariff regimes and shifts in electric-vehicle and emission-related policy in the United States and Europe as prompting clients to recalibrate technology roadmaps and sourcing strategies. As at the date of the Report the Company had NOT observed a significant impact on client programs from prevailing conflicts, with clients focused on rationalising costs while continuing to fund future programs - a stated absence that is itself a finding - but a prolonged escalation could over time influence spending in some segments more than others. Mitigation includes a global delivery model with local talent, regular review of regulatory and especially immigration-law changes, and continuous monitoring of geopolitical developments.
- Liability from client contracts — Ineffective client relationships or inability to deliver in accordance with contractual requirements may impact core operations and revenues or create additional costs, and may culminate in claims for damages by clients that adversely affect profit margins. Mitigation is robust contract governance, scrupulous review of client contracts with clearly defined scope, deliverables and client dependencies, multi-layered governance for review and approvals, appropriate risk covers, strengthened programme management and global delivery management, and continuous monitoring of key deliveries, client satisfaction scores and long-disputed outstandings to gauge claim probability.
- IT infrastructure availability and cyber security — Cyber security and IT infrastructure availability are critical to operations; inability to provide a secure environment protecting sensitive and confidential business, client and stakeholder information may impact operations and attract regulatory penalties. Mitigation is a comprehensive cyber security framework and policy, continuous investment and threat surveillance, periodic Information Security training for all employees and partners, third-party audits, and a Business Continuity Plan.
- Intellectual property infringement - in both directions, heightened by AI — The Company may infringe third-party IP through intentional or inadvertent actions of employees working on projects, risking litigation, large penalties and reputational damage - with increased probability because of AI-based technologies and digital development tools. It may equally face infringement of KPIT IP by third parties, affecting ownership rights and revenues. Mitigation is employee confidentiality undertakings and training, a periodically externally-reviewed IP infringement policy, an IP management framework, continuous assessment of IP and data risk arising from AI, access controls, and an IP governance process covering KPIT, customer, partner and third-party IP.
- Data privacy — The Company holds personal data as part of its business operations; vulnerabilities in the flow of data may lead to breach of personally identifiable information (PII). outlook.body:
- Four stated growth pillars: building a future-ready Technology MOAT (AI-led engineering + solutions & products + strategic M&A); expanding growth frontiers (geographies + verticals + adjacencies); amplifying impact through ecosystem leadership (trusted partnerships + alliances + co-innovation); and embedding sustainability into business (EcoVoyage 2030 + ESG).
- Three declared priorities of the last two years: deepening client relationships through greater ownership of complex programs and outcome-based engagements; scaling AI-led solutions and products that drive differentiation; and building an ecosystem of technology partners across chip to cloud.
- Three growth horizons: (1) go deeper and wider in the existing client base, deliberately diversifying beyond passenger-car OEMs into trucks and off-highway and breaking through with other large OEMs; (2) expand into new geographies and businesses - a leadership role in India, a strengthened presence in China to learn from the world's most competitive mobility market, and an expanding footprint across the Middle East and Africa; (3) sense and scan frontier deep-tech adjacencies (micromobility, robotics, aerospace, space), entering only where the spend is large, genuinely tech-enabled, and leadership is attainable.
- Pivot from a service-led model towards solutions, products and AI-driven services, with capabilities actively realigned to support the transition.
- Beacon - the home-grown mobility-intelligence AI platform for AI-first development, integration and validation - positioned at the centre of the strategy, built on insights from more than 2,000 production programs and being deployed across multiple global OEMs.
- Capability building through focused M&A alongside organic build: Cymotive (automotive cybersecurity) and Caresoft (vehicle engineering, manufacturing engineering, benchmarking and cost optimisation).
- Shift of commercial model towards fixed-price and outcome-based contracting, with more than 70% of new contracts now fixed-price.
- Build resilience by design - diversify across client segments, expand into new mobility markets, strengthen global delivery capability and increase outcome-based engagements, so the organisation grows through disruption rather than being knocked off course by it.
- Integrate converging disciplines (software, electronics, systems engineering, validation, manufacturing engineering and AI) into complete engineering solutions as the differentiator, and take ownership of larger, multi-domain engineering programmes.
- Broaden the delivery and talent footprint: new technology centres established in Sweden and Tunisia during FY26, plus expansion into micromobility and light electric vehicles.
- Scale reusable engineering platforms, full validation suites and AI-enabled delivery workflows to improve engineering productivity, reduce programme risk and accelerate customer development cycles.
- Quality strategy anchored on Zero Defect Delivery, a 'First Time Right' mindset, CI/CD coverage across all projects with product KPIs aligned to Automotive SPICE, and an Agile methodology aligned to SAFe and compliant to Automotive SPICE (the introduction of agile roles is stated to have enabled headcount optimisation and improved billability).
- Continuously adopt emerging standards: after aligning to ISO 21434 and the latest ISO 26262 and achieving CSMS and FSMS certifications, incorporate ISO 8800 (Safety and AI), ISO 42000 (AI Management System) and ISO 24089 (Software Update Management System).
- Sustainability embedded as strategy - EcoVoyage plus science-based targets, with a commitment to becoming a net-zero organisation by the end of this decade; social work anchored on the three E's of environment, education and energy.

outlook.body: KPIT is an asset-light engineering-services and software-products business; its expansion is footprint, delivery-capacity and platform build-out rather than plant capacity. During FY26 the Company opened its first technology centre in the Nordics at Lindholmen Science Park, Gothenburg, Sweden, positioned to deepen collaboration with European OEMs and Sweden's R&D ecosystem, and inaugurated a new software engineering centre in Tunisia as a centre of excellence for global OEM programs, with approximately 400 employees inducted and active university engagement (ENIS). The year is described as one of deliberate capability-building through targeted M&A, expanding the footprint in trucks, off-highway, gaming and cybersecurity, alongside new and deepened partnerships across passenger cars, commercial vehicles, off-highway and micromobility - including HMC HIVE (a Hero Motors company) on next-generation light electric vehicles for first- and last-mile micromobility, JSW Motors on the software and digital backbone for its New Energy Vehicle portfolio, Microsoft as AI infrastructure partner powering KPIT's Agentic AI solutions, a leading Japanese Tier 1 for next-generation digital cockpit platforms with KPIT as end-to-end integration anchor, a global off-highway equipment and machinery leader for platform-led migration to a modular software-defined electronics architecture, and a European OEM group for a long-term, large-scale engagement spanning infotainment, propulsion, vehicle engineering, body & chassis, middleware and cloud. On the infrastructure side, the Company has established a hybrid AI landscape - a small-scale AI setup inside KPIT's on-premises data centre complemented by expansion into hyper-scaler cloud environments - designed with scalable power infrastructure for high-energy AI/HPC workloads, advanced cooling, high-performance compute, tool/framework interoperability and a consistent security framework across on-premises and cloud. Other build-out during the period: migration of ERP and HRMS applications and data from on-premises to a cloud-based resilient container platform with CI/CD pipelines and monitoring/logging; completion of the next-generation disaggregated hyper-converged infrastructure (dHCI) project introduced in mid-2023, allowing compute and storage to scale independently; around 90% of critical workload now running on HCI infrastructure, with power, cooling and space savings of an additional 30% and an asset ratio optimised from 7 to 1 for the same compute capacity; a 50% increase in open-source VDI for test and training requirements; a Smart Campus platform integrating fourteen building-management systems and sensor-driven devices into a single dashboard, with a desk-reservation and visitor-management system; a virtual platform for vehicle simulation and validation built on a resilient container platform with distributed event-streaming clusters and Jenkins CI/CD; and a stated initiative to purchase equipment only from sustainability-certified OEMs. R&D output commercialised during the year includes hydrogen fuel cell technology for automotive, marine and stationary storage applications, traction motor and controller technology for automotive and marine applications (stated as delivering high efficiency, compact volume, lower cost and zero dependency on rare-earth permanent magnets imported from countries such as China), and equipment to perform R&D in fuel cell technology and traction motors. NOTE ON A BOUNDARY: the EcoVoyage sustainability paragraph in this bundle is cut off mid-sentence at 'KPIT is aligning its near-term (2030) and long-', so the near-term/long-term target framing that follows is not available here.

outlook.body:
- The automobile is no longer defined primarily by hardware - it is increasingly becoming a software and AI-defined product, and the largest mobility companies are restructuring themselves around that reality (stated as the core structural demand driver).
- As software content and system complexity continue to rise, OEMs need trusted partners who can manage the full mobility technology stack.
- OEMs are operating amid rising competitive pressures, particularly from China, and heightened geopolitical uncertainty; over the last six months these challenges have been further accentuated by supply-chain disruptions and softer market demand in several regions.
- FY26 growth was supported by strong momentum in Trucks & Off-Highway and in cloud-based connected services, with a strong fourth quarter despite a muted industry environment.
- Entering FY27 in a turbulent environment: two of the largest software-defined-vehicle programs wind down in the first half, with the revenue drop expected to be made up to some extent by growth in newly acquired accounts and solid momentum from Trucks & Off-Highway, India and China.
- Continued investment in AI, solutions, products and competencies means profitability may remain within a narrow range in the near term.
- Over the medium term, solutions and products are expected to contribute an increasing share of revenue, per-person value to improve, and profitability to strengthen.
- AI in mobility engineering must satisfy demanding standards of safety, traceability, reliability and governance - unlike many industries - which management frames as the opportunity Beacon is built for.
- Disruption is described as the operating environment rather than the exception: pandemic aftermath, supply-chain disruption, geopolitical uncertainty, changing technology roadmaps, cost pressures and the rapid emergence of AI continue to reshape mobility companies' priorities and investment decisions.
- India is described as on its way to becoming one of the world's most important automotive markets.
- New deal wins remained healthy during FY26 (qualitative; no order-book value disclosed).
- Solutions and products now account for 21% of the pipeline, reinforcing the strategic pivot underway.
- More than 70% of new contracts are fixed-price.
- More than twenty consecutive quarters of revenue and EBITDA growth, together with the increasing proportion of fixed-price and solution-led engagements, are cited as evidence of execution discipline.

risks.note: The Company's current revenues are generated from the automotive and mobility ecosystem and in particular the passenger-car segment. The cyclical nature of, or disruption in, the automotive industry, cost pressures, global slowdown and regulatory changes globally can hit growth and profitability. This is the AR's own top-listed risk and it is a structural concentration, not a cyclical one: the Company's stated differentiator - singular focus on mobility - is the same thing as its concentration. Mitigation is monitoring industry software spend and AI adoption, creating differentiated offerings, evaluating adjacent verticals, new geographies and market-specific solutions, aligning investment to client software spend, and partnerships for specific skills. The CEO's letter puts a near-term edge on it: two of the largest software-defined-vehicle programs wind down in H1 FY27.

risks.note: Technology changes and the emergence of new and disruptive technologies, especially AI, can disrupt the Company's own business model. The Board's Report is explicit that AI-led adoption may in the near term MODERATE activity in certain service areas - i.e. the Company's own AI deployment can cannibalise billable effort before it pays back. Mitigation is investment in technology competencies with a major focus on AI reviewed through Practice Development Forums, continuous evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies and AI-infused business models, new offerings, and periodic strengthening of product strategy for development, validation and networking tools supporting clients' SDV transition.
risks.risk: Technology disruption, especially AI, to the business model itself

risks.note: The work KPIT does is critical to clients' production programs; delays may impact those production programs, in an industry becoming more competitive with stricter vehicle safety and emission regulation, energy pressures and slower demand. Mitigation is agile delivery models, competency building with a focus on AI, zero-defect delivery, SCALE through automation and engineering productivity, proactive planning and process automation, and multi-level delivery reviews. The commercial mix amplifies this: more than 70% of new contracts are fixed-price, so execution slippage lands on KPIT's margin rather than the client's.
risks.risk: Delivery excellence - programme execution risk on client production programs

risks.note: Ability to attract and retain talent, especially competence in new technology areas including AI, is key to maintaining leadership. The growing trajectory of Global Capability Centers in recent years may also create a challenge in retaining key talent; higher attrition may impact delivery and the ability to pursue growth opportunities. Mitigation is a strengthened talent acquisition and retention framework, continuous training and certification including AI, leadership development programs and individual development plans, and an employee engagement and recognition framework focused on top talent.

risks.note: Inability to execute strategy will impact growth; OEMs driving major business through their own Global Capability Centers may also hit the Company's growth. This is the disintermediation risk - the client insourcing the work. Mitigation is strong strategic relationships with OEMs and top clients, a 'strategy for disrupters', a client engagement transformation program with proactive propositions and AI-infused solutions, understanding client technology roadmaps to prioritise investments, and a strategy for new offerings focused on Commercial Vehicles and Off-Highway verticals.

risks.note: Both the Company and its clients have a global footprint. Slowdown or recession in key geographies, prolonged geopolitical conflicts, trade-policy changes, supply-chain disruption and inflationary pressure may raise the cost of doing business and influence client decisions and spend. The Board's Report singles out evolving tariff regimes and shifts in electric-vehicle and emission-related policy in the United States and Europe as prompting clients to recalibrate technology roadmaps and sourcing strategies. risks.risk: Disruption in the mobility industry - single-industry and passenger-car concentration
risks.note: The Company's current revenues are generated from the automotive and mobility ecosystem and in particular the passenger-car segment. The cyclical nature of, or disruption in, the automotive industry, cost pressures, global slowdown and regulatory changes globally can hit growth and profitability. This is the AR's own top-listed risk and it is a structural concentration, not a cyclical one: the Company's stated differentiator - singular focus on mobility - is the same thing as its concentration. Mitigation is monitoring industry software spend and AI adoption, creating differentiated offerings, evaluating adjacent verticals, new geographies and market-specific solutions, aligning investment to client software spend, and partnerships for specific skills. The CEO's letter puts a near-term edge on it: two of the largest software-defined-vehicle programs wind down in H1 FY27.

risks.risk: Technology disruption, especially AI, to the business model itself
risks.note: Technology changes and the emergence of new and disruptive technologies, especially AI, can disrupt the Company's own business model. The Board's Report is explicit that AI-led adoption may in the near term MODERATE activity in certain service areas - i.e. the Company's own AI deployment can cannibalise billable effort before it pays back. Mitigation is investment in technology competencies with a major focus on AI reviewed through Practice Development Forums, continuous evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies and AI-infused business models, new offerings, and periodic strengthening of product strategy for development, validation and networking tools supporting clients' SDV transition.

risks.risk: Delivery excellence - programme execution risk on client production programs
risks.note: The work KPIT does is critical to clients' production programs; delays may impact those production programs, in an industry becoming more competitive with stricter vehicle safety and emission regulation, energy pressures and slower demand. Mitigation is agile delivery models, competency building with a focus on AI, zero-defect delivery, SCALE through automation and engineering productivity, proactive planning and process automation, and multi-level delivery reviews. The commercial mix amplifies this: more than 70% of new contracts are fixed-price, so execution slippage lands on KPIT's margin rather than the client's.

risks.risk: Top talent retention and attraction
risks.note: Ability to attract and retain talent, especially competence in new technology areas including AI, is key to maintaining leadership. The growing trajectory of Global Capability Centers in recent years may also create a challenge in retaining key talent; higher attrition may impact delivery and the ability to pursue growth opportunities. Mitigation is a strengthened talent acquisition and retention framework, continuous training and certification including AI, leadership development programs and individual development plans, and an employee engagement and recognition framework focused on top talent.

risks.risk: Inability to grow key clients / revenue concentration, including the OEM Global Capability Centre threat
risks.note: Inability to execute strategy will impact growth; OEMs driving major business through their own Global Capability Centers may also hit the Company's growth. This is the disintermediation risk - the client insourcing the work. Mitigation is strong strategic relationships with OEMs and top clients, a 'strategy for disrupters', a client engagement transformation program with proactive propositions and AI-infused solutions, understanding client technology roadmaps to prioritise investments, and a strategy for new offerings focused on Commercial Vehicles and Off-Highway verticals.

risks.risk: Profitability compression from client spending patterns, pricing pressure and people cost
risks.note: Profitability is significantly influenced by clients' spending patterns, competitive pricing pressure and increasing employee and other operational costs; lower profitability may impact sustainability and future investments. People cost is stated as the Company's significant cost. Mitigation is a focus on solutions and products, productivity improvement through AI and the employee pyramid, leveraging the global delivery model with an increase in offshore and nearshore mix, and investment in AI solutions, tools and automation.

risks.risk: Major currency fluctuation - foreign-exchange exposure on overwhelmingly overseas revenue
risks.note: Significant currency fluctuations impact financial results, and the Board's Report notes the Company's significant exposure to overseas revenues, so FX moves may affect revenues, profitability and overall financial performance; exposure extends to broader commodity trends including gold, crude oil and energy prices as drivers of currency volatility. Mitigation is a board-approved prudent forex hedging policy reviewed periodically, implementation overseen by the CFO, appropriate hedging product selection, continuous monitoring of currency movements and periodic recalibration of hedge positions.

risks.risk: Economic and political risk, global trade policy and geopolitical conflict
risks.note: Both the Company and its clients have a global footprint. Slowdown or recession in key geographies, prolonged geopolitical conflicts, trade-policy changes, supply-chain disruption and inflationary pressure may raise the cost of doing business and influence client decisions and spend. The Board's Report singles out evolving tariff regimes and shifts in electric-vehicle and emission-related policy in the United States and Europe as prompting clients to recalibrate technology roadmaps and sourcing strategies. As at the date of the Report the Company had NOT observed a significant impact on client programs from prevailing conflicts, with clients focused on rationalising costs while continuing to fund future programs - a stated absence that is itself a finding - but a prolonged escalation could over time influence spending in some segments more than others. Mitigation includes a global delivery model with local talent, regular review of regulatory and especially immigration-law changes, and continuous monitoring of geopolitical developments.

risks.risk: Liability from client contracts
risks.note: Ineffective client relationships or inability to deliver in accordance with contractual requirements may impact core operations and revenues or create additional costs, and may culminate in claims for damages by clients that adversely affect profit margins. Mitigation is robust contract governance, scrupulous review of client contracts with clearly defined scope, deliverables and client dependencies, multi-layered governance for review and approvals, appropriate risk covers, strengthened programme management and global delivery management, and continuous monitoring of key deliveries, client satisfaction scores and long-disputed outstandings to gauge claim probability.

risks.risk: IT infrastructure availability and cyber security
risks.note: Cyber security and IT infrastructure availability are critical to operations; inability to provide a secure environment protecting sensitive and confidential business, client and stakeholder information may impact operations and attract regulatory penalties. Mitigation is a comprehensive cyber security framework and policy, continuous investment and threat surveillance, periodic Information Security training for all employees and partners, third-party audits, and a Business Continuity Plan.

risks.risk: Intellectual property infringement - in both directions, heightened by AI
risks.note: The Company may infringe third-party IP through intentional or inadvertent actions of employees working on projects, risking litigation, large penalties and reputational damage - with increased probability because of AI-based technologies and digital development tools. It may equally face infringement of KPIT IP by third parties, affecting ownership rights and revenues. Mitigation is employee confidentiality undertakings and training, a periodically externally-reviewed IP infringement policy, an IP management framework, continuous assessment of IP and data risk arising from AI, access controls, and an IP governance process covering KPIT, customer, partner and third-party IP.

capex_expansion.body: KPIT is an asset-light engineering-services and software-products business; its expansion is footprint, delivery-capacity and platform build-out rather than plant capacity. During FY26 the Company opened its first technology centre in the Nordics at Lindholmen Science Park, Gothenburg, Sweden, positioned to deepen collaboration with European OEMs and Sweden's R&D ecosystem, and inaugurated a new software engineering centre in Tunisia as a centre of excellence for global OEM programs, with approximately 400 employees inducted and active university engagement (ENIS). The year is described as one of deliberate capability-building through targeted M&A, expanding the footprint in trucks, off-highway, gaming and cybersecurity, alongside new and deepened partnerships across passenger cars, commercial vehicles, off-highway and micromobility - including HMC HIVE (a Hero Motors company) on next-generation light electric vehicles for first- and last-mile micromobility, JSW Motors on the software and digital backbone for its New Energy Vehicle portfolio, Microsoft as AI infrastructure partner powering KPIT's Agentic AI solutions, a leading Japanese Tier 1 for next-generation digital cockpit platforms with KPIT as end-to-end integration anchor, a global off-highway equipment and machinery leader for platform-led migration to a modular software-defined electronics architecture, and a European OEM group for a long-term, large-scale engagement spanning infotainment, propulsion, vehicle engineering, body & chassis, middleware and cloud. On the infrastructure side, the Company has established a hybrid AI landscape - a small-scale AI setup inside KPIT's on-premises data centre complemented by expansion into hyper-scaler cloud environments - designed with scalable power infrastructure for high-energy AI/HPC workloads, advanced cooling, high-performance compute, tool/framework interoperability and a consistent security framework across on-premises and cloud. Other build-out during the period: migration of ERP and HRMS applications and data from on-premises to a cloud-based resilient container platform with CI/CD pipelines and monitoring/logging; completion of the next-generation disaggregated hyper-converged infrastructure (dHCI) project introduced in mid-2023, allowing compute and storage to scale independently; around 90% of critical workload now running on HCI infrastructure, with power, cooling and space savings of an additional 30% and an asset ratio optimised from 7 to 1 for the same compute capacity; a 50% increase in open-source VDI for test and training requirements; a Smart Campus platform integrating fourteen building-management systems and sensor-driven devices into a single dashboard, with a desk-reservation and visitor-management system; a virtual platform for vehicle simulation and validation built on a resilient container platform with distributed event-streaming clusters and Jenkins CI/CD; and a stated initiative to purchase equipment only from sustainability-certified OEMs. R&D output commercialised during the year includes hydrogen fuel cell technology for automotive, marine and stationary storage applications, traction motor and controller technology for automotive and marine applications (stated as delivering high efficiency, compact volume, lower cost and zero dependency on rare-earth permanent magnets imported from countries such as China), and equipment to perform R&D in fuel cell technology and traction motors. themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
